dossier.purpose: SGLang is an open-source serving engine for large language, multimodal and diffusion models. `sglang serve` or `python -m sglang.launch_server` starts a FastAPI/uvicorn server (default 127.0.0.1:30000) with OpenAI-, Anthropic- and Ollama-compatible HTTP APIs plus a native /generate API; `sglang.Engine` runs the same runtime in-process (README.md:65-66; python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/http_server.py:1769-2082; python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/fields/serving.py:65-66). Against the six listed needs, the repo supplies facts only for the last one (local model server): it is an NVIDIA CUDA 13 build, and the RTX 4090 (sm_89) is inside the documented 'sm80 and above' range but is not named in the README or the LLM cookbook. For the other five needs SGLang is an emitter, not a pipeline component: it can export OTLP traces (opt-in) and expose Prometheus metrics for scraping. It has no OTLP receiver, no OTLP metrics/logs exporter, no privacy-filter processor, no metrics/logs store, no general dashboard tool (only an example Grafana dashboard for its own metrics) and no trace/dataset/experiment store. It does ship a load-generating benchmark client with replayable dataset loaders (python/sglang/benchmark/).

claims.claim: SGLang is 'a high-performance serving framework for large language models and multimodal models', delivering low-latency, high-throughput inference 'from a single GPU to large distributed clusters'.

Core features listed: RadixAttention prefix caching, zero-overhead CPU scheduler, prefill-decode disaggregation, speculative decoding, continuous batching, paged attention, TP/PP/EP/DP parallelism, structured outputs, chunked prefill, quantization (FP4/FP8/INT4/AWQ/GPTQ), multi-LoRA batching.
Broad model support (language, embedding, reward and diffusion models); 'Compatible with most Hugging Face models and OpenAI APIs'.
Hardware support: NVIDIA GPUs (GB200/B300/H100/A100/Spark/5090), AMD GPUs (MI355/MI300), Intel Xeon CPUs, Google TPUs, Ascend NPUs 'and more'. The RTX 4090 is not named.

Getting started is by link only (Install, Quick Start, Cookbook with 'the deployment command we recommend for each supported model', Backend/Frontend tutorials); the README itself contains no install command.
Performance is documented by link to release blogs; the README contains no measurements of its own.

News items assert performance results: 'Unlocking 25x Inference Performance with SGLang on NVIDIA GB300 NVL72' and 'Reaching 500 TPS in two weeks' for GLM5.2 NVFP4 agentic workloads (linked blogs not opened).
SGLang is hosted under the non-profit open-source organization LMSYS.
Design and code reused from Guidance, vLLM, LightLLM, FlashInfer, Outlines and LMQL.

The README makes no statement about telemetry or network behaviour, OTLP, MCP, Anthropic/Claude Code/Codex compatibility, platform support beyond the hardware list, or security reporting (absence of claims).

install.method: pip or uv from PyPI (Linux, CUDA 13; Python 3.10+)
install.command: pip install --upgrade pip && pip install uv && uv pip install --prerelease=allow sglang

install.method: Nightly wheel from the SGLang wheel index
install.command: pip install --upgrade pip && pip install uv && uv pip install --prerelease=allow --index-strategy unsafe-best-match --extra-index-url https://docs.sglang.ai/whl/cu130/ sglang

install.method: From source (Linux, CUDA); docs pin v0.5.18, and the build needs cargo unless SGLANG_BUILD_RUST_EXTS=none
install.command: git clone -b v0.5.18 https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang.git && cd sglang && pip install --upgrade pip && pip install -e "python"

install.method: Docker (CUDA 13 image; latest and dev are mutable tags; a smaller latest-runtime variant is documented)
install.command: docker run --gpus all --shm-size 32g -p 30000:30000 -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface --env "HF_TOKEN=<secret>" --ipc=host lmsysorg/sglang:latest python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000

install.method: docker compose (copy docker/compose.yaml locally; it sets privileged: true and network_mode: host)
macOS Apple Silicon (MLX backend), from source only; replaces python/pyproject.toml with pyproject_other.toml
install.command: git clone https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang.git && cd sglang && uv venv -p 3.12 sglang-metal && source sglang-metal/bin/activate && uv pip install --upgrade pip && rm -f python/pyproject.toml && mv python/pyproject_other.toml python/pyproject.toml && uv pip install -e "python[all_mps]"  # then: SGLANG_USE_MLX=1 python -m sglang.launch_server --model MODEL_ID_OR_PATH --disable-cuda-graph --host 0.0.0.0

platforms.linux_x86_64: yes - primary target. Docs call Linux recommended and require NVIDIA CUDA 13 (docs/docs/get-started/quickstart.mdx:20-22; docs/docs/get-started/install.mdx:33-35). CI builds PyPI wheels for x86_64 on Python 3.10-3.13 (.github/workflows/release-pypi.yml:17-25) and amd64 Docker images on nvidia/cuda:13.0.3-cudnn-devel-ubuntu24.04 (docker/Dockerfile:1-2; .github/workflows/_docker-build-and-publish.yml:106-128).
platforms.wsl2: unknown - no WSL2 install or support statement for the LLM server in the README or docs, and no Windows/WSL workflow in .github. Only incidental mentions: a MiniMax-H3 diffusion cookbook hint 'on Windows run under WSL2' (docs/src/snippets/configs/MiniMaxAI/minimax-h3.jsx:175) and an AMD ROCm env var for WSL (docker/rocm-gfx1151.Dockerfile:44).
platforms.macos_arm64: yes, with caveats - separate MLX backend, source install only: Apple Silicon, macOS 14+, torch 2.13.x, MLX 0.32.0+; requires swapping python/pyproject.toml for python/pyproject_other.toml and installing extra all_mps (docs/docs/hardware-platforms/apple_metal.mdx:7-55; python/pyproject_other.toml:180-188,221). CI: .github/workflows/pr-test-mlx.yml:75,128. No CUDA on macOS; the default python/pyproject.toml pins CUDA 13 packages (:24-103).
platforms.gpu: yes for NVIDIA CUDA 13 only (docs/docs/get-started/install.mdx:33-35). RTX 4090 (Ada, sm_89, 24 GB) is within the documented 'sm80 and above, e.g., A10, A100, L4, L40S, H100' (docs/docs/get-started/quickstart.mdx:21) but is not named in README.md:71 or any LLM cookbook page (the autoregressive cookbook names H200, RTX PRO 6000, RTX 5090, DGX Spark; the 4090 appears only in diffusion cookbooks). Code evidence for sm_89: AOT kernel gencode compute_89, on by default on x86_64 (python/sglang/kernels/aot/CMakeLists.txt:99-107,196-200); CUTLASS Sm89 FP8 GEMM (python/sglang/kernels/aot/csrc/gemm/fp8_gemm_kernel.cu:90); INT8 dispatch for RTX 4090 (.../int8_gemm_kernel.cu:282); memory-tier defaults naming 4090 (python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/memory_hook.py:100-116); two fused-MoE configs for NVIDIA_GeForce_RTX_4090 (python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/configs/triton_3_1_0/). CUDA CI runners are 5090/H100/H200/B200/B300/GB300/H20 only (scripts/ci/runner_configs.yml:21-30), so no sm_89 runner. No minimum NVIDIA driver is stated in the repo.

integrations.cli: yes - console scripts `sglang` (serve | generate | version) and `killall_sglang` (python/pyproject.toml:213-215; python/sglang/cli/main.py:20-57); `python -m sglang.launch_server` (python/sglang/launch_server.py:70-86); benchmark CLI `python -m sglang.benchmark.serving` (python/sglang/bench_serving.py:1-22 is a deprecated shim).
integrations.mcp: none found as a server - SGLang does not expose itself over MCP. Client side only: Python MCPToolServer for GPT-OSS/Responses tools via mcp.client.sse (python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/tool_server.py:8-12,87) and a native MCP client in the separate Rust gateway (sgl-model-gateway/README.md:37,251-263; sgl-model-gateway/Cargo.toml:95-102).
integrations.sdk_or_api: yes - HTTP API (python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/http_server.py): OpenAI-compatible /v1/completions, /v1/chat/completions, /v1/embeddings, /v1/models, /v1/responses (:1769-1971); Anthropic-compatible POST /v1/messages and /v1/messages/count_tokens (:2065-2082); Ollama-compatible /api/chat, /api/generate, /api/tags, /api/show (:2036-2059); native /generate (:910-915); /health; Prometheus /metrics with --enable-metrics. Optional native gRPC via --grpc-port (python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/fields/serving.py:79-85). Python SDK: sglang.Engine (offline, no HTTP; python/sglang/__init__.py:68; docs/docs/get-started/quickstart.mdx:250-274) and the frontend language sglang.lang (python/sglang/__init__.py:25-64). Optional --api-key accepts only an Authorization Bearer header and exempts /health, /ready, /metrics (python/sglang/srt/utils/auth.py:98-117).
integrations.claude_code_or_codex: Claude Code: yes, documented - docs/docs/basic_usage/anthropic_api.mdx:182-253 (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER=0 required for prefix-cache reuse; the recommended env set also includes CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1, which that page describes as dropping autoupdater/telemetry/error-reporting traffic and says nothing about Claude Code OTLP export). The endpoint is registered unconditionally (python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/http_server.py:350-353,2065); tool calls need --tool-call-parser (anthropic_api.mdx:51-54,266-269); tests: test/registered/unit/entrypoints/anthropic/test_serving.py and test/registered/openai_server/function_call/test_anthropic_tool_use.py. Codex: none found - no doc or code mention; a /v1/responses endpoint exists (http_server.py:1971) but is not documented for Codex.

readme.telemetry_and_network: No phone-home, usage-statistics, analytics or crash-reporting code found: grepping python/sglang/srt for telemetry|analytics|sentry|posthog|mixpanel|usage_stats|do_not_track returns only OpenTelemetry tracing code and OpenAI-style continuous_usage_stats fields (e.g. python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/utils.py:258-264). The only hard-coded third-party service in the server is https://api.exa.ai for the optional GPT-OSS web_search tool, used only with a user-supplied EXA_API_KEY (python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/search/exa_client.py:11; python/sglang/srt/environ.py:750-753). Model, tokenizer and config files are downloaded at launch from Hugging Face Hub via huggingface_hub, which honours HF_HUB_OFFLINE (python/sglang/srt/model_loader/weight_utils.py:324-331,663-687), or from ModelScope when SGLANG_USE_MODELSCOPE is set (python/sglang/srt/environ.py:291); HF_TOKEN is needed only for gated models (docs/docs/get-started/install.mdx:72). No account is required to run. The benchmark tool can fetch Mooncake trace files from raw.githubusercontent.com (python/sglang/benchmark/datasets/common.py:14-17), and the frontend Crusoe backend has a default hosted URL (python/sglang/lang/backend/crusoe.py:7), both only when selected. Requests that carry media URLs make the server fetch them from any host unless --allowed-media-domains is set (python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/fields/mm.py:82-87). OTLP: SGLang emits OTLP traces only, opt-in via --enable-trace (default off), endpoint default localhost:4317, gRPC exporter hard-coded insecure=True, http/protobuf selectable with OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_PROTOCOL; needs the tracing extra (python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/fields/observability.py:164-172; python/sglang/srt/observability/trace.py:233-285; python/pyproject.toml:148-153). Span attributes are token counts, sampling parameters, request id, model name, finish reason, latencies and host machine-id/pid; no prompt or completion text found (python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py:3721-3788; trace.py:189-206,399-405). There is no OTLP metrics or logs exporter and no OTLP receiver in python/sglang, so it cannot be the local OTLP collector or privacy filter for Claude Code or Codex telemetry; the Rust gateway likewise only exports traces (sgl-model-gateway/Cargo.toml:64-67). Metrics: Prometheus pull endpoint /metrics only with --enable-metrics (default off; python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/http_server.py:296-297), unauthenticated even when --api-key is set (python/sglang/srt/utils/auth.py:98-106). Logging: request contents are not logged by default (--log-requests off; observability.py:36-39; docs/docs/advanced_features/observability.mdx:17); opt-in --log-requests, --export-metrics-to-file, request dump and --crash-dump-folder write request data to local files. Example stack in examples/monitoring/: Prometheus scraping 127.0.0.1:30000 (prometheus.yaml:6-10) with a Prometheus-only Grafana datasource (grafana/datasources/datasource.yaml:1-8), and an OpenTelemetry Collector plus Jaeger compose (tracing_compose.yaml:1-21) whose collector config has only a batch processor, no filtering or redaction, exports traces to Jaeger and /tmp/otel_trace.json, and routes metrics and logs pipelines only to the same Jaeger OTLP endpoint (opentelemetry.yaml:8-38).

entry_points.what: `sglang` console script (serve | generate | version), registered in python/pyproject.toml:213-215 together with `killall_sglang` (python/sglang/cli/killall.py).
`sglang serve <model>` dispatcher with a backend registry ('llm' and 'diffusion'), auto-detected from the model path.
`python -m sglang.launch_server`; run_server() picks HTTP (default), legacy SMG gRPC, Ray or encoder-only mode (lines 17-67).
FastAPI app and launch_server(): OpenAI /v1/*, Anthropic /v1/messages, Ollama /api/*, /generate, /health, admin and weight-update routes, Prometheus and API-key middleware.
In-process `sglang.Engine` (offline API, no HTTP), exported lazily from python/sglang/__init__.py:68.
Benchmark / load-generator CLI (`python -m sglang.benchmark.serving`); python/sglang/bench_serving.py is a deprecated shim.

Separate Rust model gateway/router binaries sgl-model-gateway, smg, amg (sgl-model-gateway/Cargo.toml:24-34); Python launcher sglang_router.launch_router is referenced in docs/docs/references/production_request_trace.mdx:36.
Diffusion runtime reached through `sglang serve` / `sglang generate` (python/sglang/cli/serve.py:111-131; python/sglang/cli/generate.py); needs the `diffusion` extra.

code.architecture: Multi-process Python runtime ('srt'). Entrypoints (python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/: http_server.py, openai/, anthropic/, ollama/, grpc_server.py, engine.py) feed TokenizerManager (srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py), then Scheduler processes (srt/managers/scheduler.py; ZMQ over ipc:// temp sockets on a single node, srt/server_args.py:686-717), then ModelRunner (srt/model_executor/model_runner.py) with model code (srt/models/), attention backends (srt/layers/attention/: flashinfer, triton, fa3, trtllm ...), quantization (srt/layers/quantization/) and KV/prefix caches (srt/mem_cache/radix_cache.py, hicache); output goes through DetokenizerManager (srt/managers/detokenizer_manager.py). Feature packages: srt/speculative/ (EAGLE, DFlash, ngram), srt/disaggregation/ (prefill/decode, encoder), srt/lora/, srt/constrained/ (xgrammar, llguidance, outlines), srt/function_call/ and srt/parser/ (tool and reasoning parsers), srt/multimodal/, srt/observability/ (Prometheus collector, OTLP trace.py, request logging in srt/utils/request_logger.py). Configuration lives in srt/server_args.py, srt/arg_groups/ and srt/environ.py (SGLANG_* variables). Kernels: python/sglang/kernels/aot (CUDA, shipped as the separate sglang-kernel wheel), kernels/jit, kernels/ops (Triton). Rust crates in rust/ (sglang-grpc, sglang-mm, sglang-renderer, sglang-server, sglang-radix-tree) are built as PyO3 extensions by python/setup.py; the Rust HTTP frontend is opt-in (SGLANG_RUST_SERVER, default off; srt/environ.py:1829). Also: frontend DSL python/sglang/lang/, diffusion runtime python/sglang/multimodal_gen/, separate Rust gateway sgl-model-gateway/, benchmarks python/sglang/benchmark/, docs and cookbook in docs/ (Mintlify).
code.packaging_and_release: PyPI wheel `sglang`: .github/workflows/release-pypi.yml runs on tag push v[0-9]+.* or manual dispatch (:2-12); matrix Python 3.10-3.13 x x86_64/aarch64 on self-hosted build nodes (:17-25); installs protoc and Rust (:47-53); `python3 -m build --wheel` (:71); auditwheel repair via scripts/release/prepare_sglang_wheel.py (:77-80); wheels only (no sdist) uploaded with twine and a PYPI_TOKEN secret from the prod environment (:88-114). Version comes from git tags via setuptools-scm (python/pyproject.toml:255-260). Tags are created by workflow_dispatch in release-tag.yml. Docker: release-docker.yml and _docker-build-and-publish.yml build linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 from docker/Dockerfile (CUDA 13.0.3, --no-cache), push by digest and merge manifests tagged v{version}, latest, v{version}-cu130, latest-cu130 (release-docker.yml:50-53; _docker-build-and-publish.yml:106-256). Kernel wheel sglang-kernel 0.4.7 (python/sglang/kernels/aot/python/sgl_kernel/version.py:1): release-whl-kernel.yml builds cu130 x86_64/aarch64, ROCm and MUSA wheels, uploads cu130 to PyPI by token and publishes to the sgl-project/whl release and index (:35-166). No signing, attestation, SBOM or published checksum step appears in any workflow (grep of .github for cosign|sigstore|attest|slsa|sbom|checksum found only a sanitizer sha256 check in release-whl-deepgemm.yml:200 and `provenance: false` in NPU Docker workflows). Nightly wheels come from the SGLang wheel index (docs/docs/get-started/install.mdx:40). docs/docs/developer_guide/release_process.mdx:9-18 describes `bash upload_pypi.sh`, which does not exist (python/upload_pypi.sh absent).
code.tests_and_ci: Frameworks: unittest and pytest (test/pytest.ini sets asyncio_mode=auto; test/README.md:18-35). Layout: test/registered/ (about 2,088 test_*.py files, 813 of them under test/registered/unit/) is auto-discovered by test/run_suite.py through register_*_ci calls; test/manual/ (about 247 test_*.py) is non-CI; about 343 more test_*.py sit under python/ (kernel and multimodal_gen tests); sgl-model-gateway/tests has 57 .rs files. Roughly 2,340 test_*.py files under test/. CI (.github/workflows): pr-test.yml (PRs plus cron twice daily; staged base-a, base-b, base-c, test/README.md:8-10), pr-test-extra.yml, pr-test-sgl-kernel.yml, pr-test-jit-kernel.yml, pr-test-multimodal-gen.yml, pr-test-rust*.yml, pr-test-amd*.yml, pr-test-npu.yml, pr-test-xpu.yml, pr-test-xeon.yml, pr-test-musa.yml, pr-test-mlx.yml (macos-26 plus self-hosted macOS ARM64), nightly-*.yml, lint.yml (pre-commit, lychee, Mintlify broken-links). CUDA runner labels: 1-gpu-5090, 1-gpu-h100, 2/4-gpu-h100, 8-gpu-h200, b200, b300, gb300, h20 (scripts/ci/runner_configs.yml:21-30); no RTX 4090 or other sm_89 runner. Maintainers may bypass flaky CI (.github/MAINTAINER.md:5,38).
code.dependencies: python/pyproject.toml: 77 direct runtime dependencies (28 exact-pinned with ==, including torch==2.13.0, transformers==5.12.1, flashinfer_python[cu13]==0.6.18, openai==2.6.1, xgrammar==0.2.7, sglang-kernel==0.4.7; several CUDA-13 specific such as cuda-python>=13.0, nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13], humming-kernels[cu13], nvshmem4py-cu13) plus 5 build-system requires (:1-9, :24-103); extras: tracing 4, diffusion 20, diffusion-qvg 2, test 23, ray 1, http2 1, fastokens 1, checkpoint-engine 1, runai 1, dev, all (:110-201). No Python lock file or requirements file for runtime. Platform variants python/pyproject_{cpu,npu,xpu,other}.toml and python/sglang/kernels/aot/pyproject*.toml were not counted. rust/Cargo.toml: workspace with 14 shared dependencies (:24-38); rust/Cargo.lock and rust/sglang-radix-tree/Cargo.lock are committed. sgl-model-gateway/Cargo.toml: 76 direct dependencies, 12 dev, 2 build (:36-147) with no committed Cargo.lock (.gitignore:232-235). Go modules under sgl-model-gateway/bindings/golang/ were not read.
code.security_policy: none - no SECURITY.md or vulnerability-reporting instructions anywhere in the checkout (globs for SECURITY* and .github/SECURITY* found nothing; grep for security policy, vulnerability reporting and security@ found nothing). The only contact is an enterprise e-mail in README.md:93-94.

claim_checks.claim: README.md:70 - 'Compatible with most Hugging Face models and OpenAI APIs'.
claim_checks.evidence: OpenAI-compatible routes are implemented (python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/http_server.py:1769-1971: /v1/completions, /v1/chat/completions, /v1/embeddings, /v1/responses; /v1/models at :1898). Anthropic (:2065-2082) and Ollama (:2036-2059) routes also exist but are not in the README. 'Most Hugging Face models' is not checkable from code; trust_remote_code defaults to False (python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/fields/model.py:98-101).

On CUDA the registry has fp8, awq, awq_marlin, gptq_marlin, modelopt_fp4, bitsandbytes, gguf (python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/__init__.py:62-90). Plain 'gptq' is registered only for NPU/CPU/XPU (:105-135) and the docs say it was 'Removed on NVIDIA and AMD GPUs - use gptq_marlin' (docs/docs/advanced_features/quantization.mdx:95-100). Native FP4 needs SM100+; on SM80-SM90 (incl. RTX 4090) NVFP4 uses a Marlin W4A16 fallback (quantization.mdx:158-162,301-308); ModelOpt FP8 is listed as Hopper/SM90+ (:151-155).

But other opt-in features persist request data: --export-metrics-to-file serializes request fields except image/video/audio data and input_embeds, and its skip-list comes from the request logger, which is empty when --log-requests is off (python/sglang/srt/observability/request_metrics_exporter.py:16-62; request_logger.py:193-233; python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py:705-709). claim_checks.claim: docs/docs/references/production_request_trace.mdx:6 - request traces are exported to an OpenTelemetry Collector via --enable-trace and --otlp-traces-endpoint.
claim_checks.evidence: python/sglang/srt/observability/trace.py:43-64,233-285 builds OTLPSpanExporter (gRPC with insecure=True, or http/protobuf) behind BatchSpanProcessor; defaults enable_trace=False and otlp_traces_endpoint='localhost:4317' (python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/fields/observability.py:164-172). Spans only: no OTLP metric or log exporter exists in python/sglang and nothing receives OTLP. Span attributes are token counts, sampling params, request id, model name, finish reason, latencies and host machine-id/pid; no prompt or completion text found (python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py:3721-3788; trace.py:189-206,399-405).

claim_checks.claim: docs quickstart.mdx:21 vs install.mdx:33,233 - GPU requirement 'sm80 and above', CUDA 13, FlashInfer 'sm75 and above'.
claim_checks.evidence: The docs give different floors (docs/docs/get-started/quickstart.mdx:21 'sm80 and above, e.g., A10, A100, L4, L40S, H100'; install.mdx:233 'FlashInfer ... only supports sm75 and above'). python/pyproject.toml pins CUDA-13 builds (:32-34,42,55,58). AOT kernels are compiled for sm_80 and sm_89 on x86_64 by default (python/sglang/kernels/aot/CMakeLists.txt:99-107,196-200). On Ada the default attention backend is flashinfer, else triton (docs/docs/advanced_features/attention_backend.mdx:548). No minimum NVIDIA driver is stated; a SageMaker note says the default AMI's drivers are incompatible with the CUDA 13 images (docs/docs/basic_usage/aws_sagemaker.mdx:137-138).

risks: Platform fit: the only supported NVIDIA path is CUDA 13 (docs/docs/get-started/install.mdx:33-35; docker/Dockerfile:1-2; the CUDA 12 lane was retired after 0.5.19). RTX 4090 (sm_89) is not named in the README or any LLM cookbook page (it appears only in diffusion cookbooks), CUDA CI has no sm_89 runner (scripts/ci/runner_configs.yml:21-30), no minimum NVIDIA driver is documented, WSL2 is undocumented for the LLM server and untested (no Windows/WSL workflow), and macOS needs a separate MLX source install that swaps pyproject files (docs/docs/hardware-platforms/apple_metal.mdx:37-55).

Install weight and drift: 77 direct runtime dependencies, 28 exact-pinned (torch==2.13.0, transformers==5.12.1, flashinfer_python[cu13]==0.6.18, openai==2.6.1, xgrammar==0.2.7, sglang-kernel==0.4.7; python/pyproject.toml:24-103) and no Python lock file, so sharing an environment with other tools is likely to conflict. Source installs need cargo, and protoc for the gRPC extension (python/setup.py:56-88; .github/workflows/release-pypi.yml:47-53), which the install page does not mention; the install page still pins v0.5.18 (install.mdx:57); latest and dev Docker tags are mutable (install.mdx:75).

Network exposure and auth defaults: the server binds 127.0.0.1 by default (python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/fields/serving.py:65), but the documented docker run and compose examples use --host 0.0.0.0, publish port 30000 and set no API key (docs/docs/get-started/install.mdx:79-86; docker/compose.yaml:19-22), and compose adds privileged: true and host networking (docker/compose.yaml:10-11). --api-key is Bearer-only and /health, /ready, /metrics stay unauthenticated (python/sglang/srt/utils/auth.py:98-117). Management routes (weight updates, cache flush, profiling, logging configuration, LoRA load/unload: http_server.py:988-1756) are ADMIN_OPTIONAL, i.e. open when no key is configured (auth.py:128-143). --allowed-media-domains is empty by default, so client-supplied media URLs are fetched from any domain (python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/fields/mm.py:82-87; python/sglang/srt/utils/common.py:1620-1631).

Privacy plumbing: SGLang is not a collector or filter. The example collector config has only a batch processor (examples/monitoring/opentelemetry.yaml:8-9), listens on 0.0.0.0:4317/4318 with those ports published (examples/monitoring/tracing_compose.yaml:7-9) and uses unpinned images. SGLang's gRPC OTLP exporter is hard-coded insecure=True (python/sglang/srt/observability/trace.py:283) and spans carry the host machine-id (trace.py:189-206,399-405). --export-metrics-to-file appears able to write request parameters, including prompt fields, when --log-requests is off (python/sglang/srt/observability/request_metrics_exporter.py:40-62; python/sglang/srt/utils/request_logger.py:193-233) - code read only, not run.

Scope and evidence gaps: no OTLP receiver, no OTLP metrics/logs export, no metrics/logs store and no experiment/dataset store; observability is Prometheus pull plus trace export only (python/sglang/srt/observability/trace.py; examples/monitoring/prometheus.yaml:6-10). Every performance number in the checkout is project-reported (see benchmarks); none is independent, and none is an LLM measurement on an RTX 4090 (closest: RTX 5090 numbers; the 4090 numbers are for a diffusion model).

Release integrity: PyPI wheels (wheels only, no sdist) are uploaded with a long-lived PYPI_TOKEN secret from self-hosted build nodes, and no signing, attestation, SBOM or published checksum step appears in any workflow (.github/workflows/release-pypi.yml:88-114; grep of .github found only a sanitizer sha256 check at release-whl-deepgemm.yml:200 and `provenance: false` in NPU Docker workflows). The Docker publish job runs the third-party action jlumbroso/free-disk-space@main, not pinned to a SHA (.github/workflows/_docker-build-and-publish.yml:80-81); the kernel release uses softprops/action-gh-release@v2 with a PAT (release-whl-kernel.yml:142-147). The base image nvidia/cuda:13.0.3-cudnn-devel-ubuntu24.04 is referenced by tag, not digest (docker/Dockerfile:1-2).

Maintenance and governance: fast-moving (docs still reference 0.5.18 and 0.5.19 while the tag is 0.5.21; CUDA 12 dropped; install.mdx:33-35,57,105); docs drift (docs/docs/developer_guide/release_process.mdx:9-18 describes `bash upload_pypi.sh`, a file that does not exist, while releases are tag-triggered); maintainers may bypass branch protection and flaky CI (.github/MAINTAINER.md:5,38); no SECURITY.md or disclosure process in the checkout.

Licensing: root licence is Apache-2.0 (LICENSE; python/pyproject.toml:17-21). Vendored subtrees carry other permissive licences: MIT (DeepSeek, python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/deep_select/vendor/LICENSE) and BSD-3-Clause (python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/flash_attn/cute/LICENSE). The Docker image is built on an NVIDIA CUDA/cuDNN base (docker/Dockerfile:1-2) whose terms were not reviewed, and model weights carry their own licences (not part of this repo; not reviewed).

checks.statement: yes for NVIDIA CUDA 13 only; RTX 4090 (sm_89) is within the documented 'sm80 and above' but is not named in README.md:71 or any LLM cookbook page (4090 only in diffusion cookbooks); sm_89 code evidence (AOT gencode, Sm89 FP8 GEMM, INT8 dispatch, memory tiers, two 4090 MoE configs); CUDA CI runners have no sm_89; no minimum NVIDIA driver stated
checks.note: Every cited line matches. CUDA 13 is required (install.mdx:33). quickstart.mdx:21 reads 'sm80 and above, e.g., A10, A100, L4, L40S, H100'. README.md:71 lists GB200/B300/H100/A100/Spark/5090, not the 4090. CMakeLists.txt adds compute_89 when ENABLE_BELOW_SM90, which is ON by default except on aarch64. fp8_gemm_kernel.cu:90 uses ArchTag Sm89. int8_gemm_kernel.cu:282 names the RTX 4090. memory_hook.py:101 has '# A10, 4090, 5090'. Both NVIDIA_GeForce_RTX_4090 fp8_w8a8 configs exist under triton_3_1_0/. '4090' appears only in diffusion docs and cookbooks, never in docs/cookbook/autoregressive, which does name H200, RTX PRO 6000, RTX 5090 and DGX Spark. No workflow runs-on label is an sm_89 GPU. Two small imprecisions don't change the finding: (1) .github/workflows/nightly-72-gpu-gb200.yml:223,276 also uses a 72-gpu-gb200 runner (not sm_89) that runner_configs.yml doesn't list; (2) two kernel-extension import errors say 'Ensure CUDA Driver >= 12.4' (python/sglang/kernels/aot/python/sgl_kernel/spatial.py:12; flash_mla.py:14), but no general minimum NVIDIA driver is documented.

checks.statement: Claude Code: yes, documented (anthropic_api.mdx:182-253; ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER=0; endpoint registered unconditionally; tool calls need --tool-call-parser; tests). Codex: none found - no doc or code mention; a /v1/responses endpoint exists (http_server.py:1971) but is not documented for Codex.
checks.note: The Claude Code half holds. anthropic_api.mdx:188-196 exports ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN. :193 and :232-245 make CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER=0 required for prefix-cache reuse. :192 and :250-252 say CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC covers only autoupdater/telemetry/error reporting, and the page never mentions OTLP. AnthropicServing is built unconditionally (http_server.py:350-353). /v1/messages and /v1/messages/count_tokens are at :2065-2082. The tool-call-parser caveat is at :51-54 and :266-269. Both cited test files exist. The Codex half is wrong as written: there are code mentions bearing directly on Codex use. test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_responses_protocol.py:108-126 builds a /v1/responses request with {type:'namespace', name:'codex', tools:[apply_patch, shell]}, and test_serving_responses.py:1077 does the same. python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/protocol.py:1722-1749 accepts 'namespace' tools with inner tools so 'clients aren't rejected'. But serving_responses.py:1181-1192 forwards only function and custom tools to the model, so tools inside a namespace are dropped. README.md:96 also mentions OpenAI Codex, but only as a contributor sponsorship, not an integration.

checks.statement: Request traces are exported to an OpenTelemetry Collector via --enable-trace and --otlp-traces-endpoint: verified yes; spans only, no OTLP metric or log exporter in python/sglang, nothing receives OTLP; span attributes are counts, sampling params, request id, model, finish reason, latencies and host machine-id/pid, no prompt or completion text.
checks.note: The doc line says exactly this. http_server.py:300-306 calls process_tracing_init(otlp_traces_endpoint) only when enable_trace is set. trace.py:245-250 wraps a BatchSpanProcessor around get_otlp_span_exporter. :272-285 picks GRPCSpanExporter(insecure=True), or the HTTP exporter when OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_PROTOCOL=http/protobuf. Defaults are enable_trace=False and otlp_traces_endpoint='localhost:4317' (observability.py:164,169-172). Span attributes are token counts, request id, sampling params, model name and finish reason (tokenizer_manager.py:3737-3783), plus host_id from /etc/machine-id and pid (trace.py:189-206,399-405). No text is attached. python/sglang has no OTLPMetricExporter, OTLPLogExporter, MeterProvider or LoggerProvider. One overstatement: 'nothing receives OTLP' is literally false. python/sglang/test/otel_collector.py is an in-memory, traces-only OTLP receiver for test assertions (gRPC on 127.0.0.1, HTTP fallback /v1/traces), and it ships in the wheel because python/pyproject.toml:231-241 excludes only top-level tests*. It is a test fixture, not a usable collector or filter, so the verified conclusion stands.

repairs: integrations.claude_code_or_codex (the statement that does not hold): replace 'Codex: none found - no doc or code mention; a /v1/responses endpoint exists (http_server.py:1971) but is not documented for Codex.' with: 'Codex: no documented integration. /v1/responses (python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/http_server.py:1971) accepts Codex-shaped requests: unwired tool types, including type "namespace" with inner tools, pass validation "so clients aren't rejected" (python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/protocol.py:1722-1749), and unit tests send a "codex" namespace containing apply_patch and shell (test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_responses_protocol.py:108-126; test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_responses.py:1064-1081). However, only function and custom tools are forwarded to the model (python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_responses.py:1181-1192), so tools inside a namespace are silently dropped. There is no Codex doc and no end-to-end Codex test. Other Codex mentions are not integrations (README.md:96 contributor sponsorship; scripts/playground/launch_pr_babysitters.sh; kernel comments).'
